annotationWithheld.clue: ASI: Holy Moses, what does this amount to !

clue.text: Cosy situations in the upholstery trade?

definitions.text: Cosy situations in the upholstery trade?

parts.words: Cosy situations in the upholstery trade?
parts.note: easy, comfortable jobs, read literally as the padded, cushioned work an upholsterer does

explanation.surface: A wry look at the comfortable life of people who stuff sofas.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy, undemanding post is idiomatically called this, and upholsterers literally work with padding.

clue.text: Uncle involved with us at the centre

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of these two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A relative and some friends find themselves the focus of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' tangles the letters of UNCLE and US together.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of an atom or cell, or anything round which things gather, is its central part.

clue.text: Proved to be Latin topics of a sort

indicators.note: to sort something is to arrange it, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shows that certain subjects are classical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges the nine letters of TOPICS OF A. The definition describes a Latin phrase meaning 'by that very fact', i.e. shown true by the fact itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means 'by the fact itself', used when something is demonstrated automatically.

clue.text: Sober geezer once till the spirits moved him

definitions.text: Sober geezer once till the spirits moved him

indicators.note: moved means shifted about, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old man stayed teetotal until ghosts changed his heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges SOBER GEEZER ONCE into fifteen letters. The whole clue describes Dickens's miser in A Christmas Carol, reformed by the visiting spirits; 'spirits' looks like drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens miser is visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve and becomes generous.

clue.text: Charge amounting to nothing on paper

definitions.text: Charge amounting to nothing on paper

parts.words: Charge amounting to nothing on paper
parts.note: an explosive load with no bullet, which does nothing, made with a paper casing; also reads as a blank cheque

explanation.surface: A bill that comes to zero when written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a bill or fee, but it is an explosive charge; a dummy round has powder in a paper wad but no shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy round holds powder but no projectile, so firing it achieves nothing.

clue.text: Knot done wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly means done incorrectly, so the letters of the word are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A tie made badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges DONE.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany or networks a junction point, like a swelling on a stem, is a knot.

clue.text: Believer in a national home, one on its resettlement to the last letter

parts.note: Z is the final letter of the alphabet
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: resettlement means moving to a new place, so the letters of the word are relocated

explanation.surface: A supporter of a homeland who is precise to the very last detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resettlement' rearranges ITS into IST; I, ON and IST are joined to Z, which leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of a Jewish homeland in Palestine were called by this name.

clue.text: Transplanted trees

indicators.note: transplanted means moved to new ground, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trees dug up and put in somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transplanted' rearranges TREES; the whole clue also describes trees put back in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants replanted in a new spot have been put in again.

clue.text: Short-lived celebrity ?

parts.note: a person currently famous whose fame may last only briefly

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names whoever is in the news right now, a transient star.

clue.text: Pendant flower, one a German botanist first named

indicators.note: first says the botanist's name comes before the other pieces

parts.note: Leonhart Fuchs was a sixteenth-century German botanist
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A drooping bloom named after an early German plant expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts FUCHS ahead of I and A; 'named' is a link, and the plant really was named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: This shrub bears hanging, bell-like blossoms, often red and purple.

clue.text: Bend in rough road unserviceable and difficult

indicators.note: in says the bend sits inside the rearranged letters
rough means roughly made, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: A curve on a bumpy, unusable road makes for hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' makes ARDO and 'in' places the bend inside; U/S is the RAF abbreviation for unserviceable, and a U-bend is a bend shaped like U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laborious and taxing is hard to do.

clue.text: Young Australian jumper with a bit of money

definitions.meaning: a baby kangaroo, a jumper from Australia
old slang for a threepenny bit, a small pre-decimal British coin

explanation.surface: A baby kangaroo carrying a small coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater but is a kangaroo. A threepenny bit was a small coin in Britain's pre-1971 money.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians name an infant kangaroo this way, and the same slang once named a threepenny coin.

clue.text: Stops in a bottleneck

parts.note: stoppers placed in the neck of a bottle, read as halts in a traffic jam

explanation.surface: Traffic halting repeatedly in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottleneck' suggests a traffic jam; it is the neck of a bottle, and the stops are stoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoppers made from bark are pushed into bottle necks to seal them.

clue.text: Said to be one of the chosen in ancient Britain

definitions.note: the definition is a member of an ancient people of northern Britain, carried by 'one' with this phrase

indicators.note: said to be means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: chosen people are picked ones

explanation.surface: An ancient Briton reputed to be one of the elect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said to be' gives a word that sounds like PICKED; 'one' serves both readings, as a picked one and an ancient Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picts were a people living in what is now Scotland in Roman and early medieval times.

clue.text: Cairo cats are out of place here

definitions.text: Cairo cats are out of place here

indicators.note: out of place means not where they belong, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Egyptian felines would look odd in this country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' rearranges CAIRO CATS; 'here' points to the Central American country the letters spell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central American republic is a country where Egyptian cats would be far from home.

clue.text: See 3
Social do thrown by Americans objecting to our brew?

definitions.text: Social do thrown by Americans objecting to our brew?

parts.words: Social do thrown by Americans objecting to our brew?
parts.note: a gathering sounds like a party, but the 1773 colonists threw British tea into the harbour in protest at its tax

explanation.surface: Americans host a gathering to protest against British tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' fits a party, but the tea itself was thrown into the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: In 1773 Massachusetts colonists dumped taxed British tea chests into the harbour.

clue.text: Detached dweller I unfairly defame

parts.note: to slander is to defame someone with false spoken words

explanation.surface: A loner admits to spreading lies about people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living on land cut off by water lives apart from the mainland.

clue.text: Where Antipodean livestock are trained?

parts.note: Australian ranches for stock, read as railway stations where animals are put on trains, echoing 'action stations'

explanation.surface: A question about where Australian farm animals are schooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' suggests schooling but means put on trains; an Australian ranch is a station.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia a large ranch is called a station, and these ones raise beef herds.

clue.text: A doubly beastly wordy involvement

parts.note: two animals: a nag is an old horse
two animals: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Something twice as horrid tangled up in verbiage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly beastly' gives two animals in a row, a horse then a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearrangement of letters makes words entangle with each other, a word puzzle.

clue.text: Birds the French pursue round a river in Spain

indicators.note: pursue means follow, so the French article comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
rio is Spanish for river
les is the French plural article meaning the

explanation.surface: French birdwatchers chase their quarry around a Spanish river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursue' sets the article last; 'round' is the letter O by its shape, and rio is simply the Spanish word for river.
explanation.definitionFit: These are songbirds, many with bright yellow and black plumage.

clue.text: Write about a kind of fur :

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pen goes round the letter

parts.note: to pen is to write

explanation.surface: An instruction to describe a type of pelt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PEN round A. In heraldry this is a fur pattern, black with gold spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldry has several tinctures called furs, and this is one, gold flecked on black.

clue.text: Problem for artist's model

definitions.meaning: a puzzling question or tricky difficulty
someone who holds a pose for a painter

explanation.surface: Trouble for a painter's sitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A baffling question is so called, as is someone striking poses for a painter.

clue.text: Malignant content of canned beef ?

indicators.note: content of means the contents inside, so the animal goes into the container

parts.note: canned food comes in a tin
beef comes from an ox

explanation.surface: Something poisonous lurking inside tinned meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' signals one piece held inside the other; the whole clue also describes a poison in spoilt tinned meat, such as botulism.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison produced by bacteria, such as botulinum in badly tinned meat, is harmful.

clue.text: See 15
Little woman in a get-together

parts.note: Jo March is a heroine of Alcott's novel Little Women

explanation.surface: A small lady at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo is one of the four March sisters in Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite or connect is to bring things together, and a junction is a meeting point.

clue.text: Established company

definitions.meaning: fixed and settled, securely in place

explanation.surface: A long-standing business.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidly fixed things are described with this word, and it also names a business.

clue.text: See 4
Grating note tormented

parts.note: a grille is a grating of bars
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A harsh musical tone that tortured listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating' looks like an adjective for the note but is a noun, a metal grating.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone questioned relentlessly is put through an ordeal, interrogated harshly.

clue.text: Rex takes roughly a minute to think it over

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: roughly means approximately or carelessly arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The king spends about sixty seconds deliberating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges A MINUTE; 'takes' joins R to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or reflect at length is to chew something over mentally.

clue.text: Bore, perhaps, but he doesn't give anything away

definitions.meaning: a drilling tool used for boring wells is so called
a stingy person who hoards money

explanation.surface: A dull man who is also tight-fisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person but points to a well-boring auger of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder of money is mean, and a well-sinker's auger shares the name.
